title: Print Lifecycle and User Experience
summary: What START_PRINT, END_PRINT, CANCEL_PRINT, M600, UI prompts, and timelapse will feel like.

content.text: Plain summary

The print experience should feel calmer and more predictable: you confirm the plate, select an approved Orca file, the printer does its own warmup, homing, mesh, park, and moving purge, then it prints. End and cancel lift before traveling and park high enough for nozzle cleaning when safe.
Printer Status action

Both Mainsail and KlipperScreen show a plainly labeled Printer Status action. It is safe to open while idle or printing because it only reads state. It shows actual and target nozzle and bed temperatures, homed axes, whether the plate is clean and rearmed, whether commissioning is still locked, and whether the filament sensor reports filament. The only prompt button is Close.

The internal command is T_STATUS rather than T300_STATUS because exact Klipper v0.13 rejects macro names containing digits. The human-facing label does not expose that implementation detail during normal use.

START_PRINT resets pressure advance before the moving purge. END_PRINT and cancellation reset it during cleanup. A failed or cancelled print also invalidates the plate-ready check so the next filament-processing action asks for a fresh cleaned-and-rearmed confirmation.
Start of print
The file must already have object metadata and approved temperatures.
You press Cleaned and rearmed before homing or print start.
The nozzle waits at a low standby temperature while the bed heats.
The printer homes through standard sensor-based Klipper behavior.
A full 9x9 mesh is generated at bed temperature.
The printer parks, heats the nozzle to final temperature, and performs KAMP moving line purge.
The first model move begins only after those checks pass.
End and cancel
END_PRINT retracts only if Klipper says the hotend can safely extrude, turns heaters and fan off, lifts first, then parks at or above Z 200 when limits allow.
CANCEL_PRINT turns heaters off first and then does optional retract and park only when state is safe.
Neither path lowers the head to reach the cleaning position.
If axes are not homed or clearance is unsafe, the macro skips movement instead of guessing.
Emergency Stop remains the immediate unsafe-condition button; ordinary Cancel can queue behind active homing, probing, or temperature waits.

attrs.title: safety questions
attrs.instruction: When do you turn the fan off exactly?  those should still be on while cooling down right?
attrs.resolution: Answered in Cooling and fans: the part-cooling fan turns off at end, cancel, and idle; the hotend heatsink fan remains Klipper temperature-controlled and should keep cooling the hotend.

content.text: Cooling and fans

There are two different fan concepts here. The part-cooling fan cools the printed plastic. The hotend heatsink fan protects the hotend by cooling the heat break. They should not be treated as one switch.

END_PRINT waits for queued moves, marks the plate dirty, retracts only if the hotend is still safe to extrude, turns heaters off, then sends M107 to turn the part-cooling fan off before the safe park message.
CANCEL_PRINT uses the pinned Mainsail client path: it shuts heaters off, sends M106 S0 for the part-cooling fan, then calls the T300 cancel hook for hot-only retract and clearance-aware parking.
Normal idle after ten minutes turns heaters off and sends M107 for the part-cooling fan, while leaving motors enabled.

The hotend heatsink fan is configured as Klipper heater_fan hotend_fan. M106 and M107 do not turn that safety fan off. It follows Klipper heater-fan behavior and should continue running while the hotend is above its cooling threshold.

For PLA, turning the part-cooling fan off at end/cancel/idle is acceptable. If a future material benefits from controlled post-print part cooling, that should be a material/profile decision, not a replacement for hotend cooling.
UI design

KlipperScreen and Mainsail are simplified around the normal user workflow: build-plate check, file selection, attended homing, print monitoring, camera, and notifications. Raw movement, heaters, extrusion, shell-like console use, machine panels, and upload-and-print shortcuts are hidden by default as mistake reduction. The real safety boundary remains the policy layer, not UI hiding.

attrs.title: unhide
attrs.instruction: hidden by default is fine but are they easy to unhide? I still would like to have easy access to advanced controls
attrs.resolution: Answered in Advanced controls access: Mainsail advanced panels are easy to reveal through normal UI customization; KlipperScreen production menus stay deliberately narrow and require a reviewed config change or maintenance mode.

content.text: Advanced controls access
Hidden by default means mistake-reduction, not owner lockout. The design is different on Mainsail and on the small KlipperScreen because the risk of a stray tap is different.

Mainsail: advanced pages and panels are hidden in the seeded defaults, but they are normal Mainsail navigation and dashboard settings. The owner can reveal Console, Machine, Heightmap, G-code Viewer, temperature, toolhead, extruder, and other panels through Mainsail layout/navigation customization on the laptop or tablet.
Mainsail macros are not globally hidden; hiddenMacros is empty. The default visible group is only Owner Actions so the normal screen stays calm, but this is not the safety boundary.

KlipperScreen: production uses an exact small menu allowlist. Advanced movement, temperature, console, mesh, updater, pins, and system panels are not meant to be one-tap-unhidden on the printer touchscreen. Adding them should be a reviewed config change or done in the separate maintenance configuration.

Revealing an advanced Mainsail panel does not bypass the scanner, t300_safety extra, hard limits, forbidden-command list, or Klipper heater/endstop/probe safeguards. It only makes allowed controls visible.
Recommended operating pattern: keep the printer touchscreen simple for printing and emergency use; use Mainsail on a larger device when you intentionally want advanced diagnostics.
Timelapse

The planned timelapse takes one non-parking frame per layer and stores frames on USB with space and frame-count preflights. If the camera or USB fails, timelapse disables itself without pausing or changing the print.
